note: Verifies OpenTofu destroy/state semantics via CLI plan verbs and process exit codes, not timing. No statistical distribution applies: for a given tofu version each scenario is a deterministic plan/apply outcome. 'to forget' and 'to destroy' are plan verbs printed by the CLI; exit codes are the process return values.
subject: opentofu 1.12.0 (re-verified identical on 1.12.3)

behaviors_verified.claim: prevent_destroy became an evaluated expression: the same config, with prevent_destroy = var.lock, is accepted by 1.12 but rejected at validate by 1.11.

observations.1.11.10: validate error: 'Variables not allowed' / 'Variables may not be used here.' — plan never runs.
observations.1.12.0: accepted; plan/apply OK, note.txt created on disk.
observations.1.12.0 destroy -var lock=true: BLOCKED: 'Resource instance cannot be destroyed' (prevent_destroy set). note.txt PRESENT. Hint suggests -exclude=, not legacy -target.
observations.1.12.0 destroy -var lock=false: ALLOWED: 'Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy' -> note.txt GONE.

behaviors_verified.changelog: #3474/#3507 (prevent_destroy may reference symbols e.g. input variables)

behaviors_verified.claim: lifecycle { destroy = false } on a managed resource turns destroy into a 'forget' that keeps the real object, and OpenTofu deliberately exits non-zero to flag the orphan.

observations.apply: keep.txt on disk + local_file.keep in state.
observations.destroy: 'Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy, 1 to forget.' — new plan verb 'forget'. keep.txt SURVIVED (orphan), state entry removed (tofu state list empty). exit code = 1, message: 'Destroy was successful but left behind forgotten instances' + '...may continue to incur charges' + suggests -suppress-forget-errors.

behaviors_verified.claim: When both destroy = false and prevent_destroy = true are set on one resource, destroy = false wins: the resource is silently forgotten, prevent_destroy does NOT block it.

observations.destroy: 'Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy, 1 to forget.' both.txt PRESENT. prevent_destroy did NOT block. Matches docs: 'prevent_destroy will not have any effect.'

behaviors_verified.footgun: A resource you believe is protected by prevent_destroy is silently forgotten if destroy = false is also present.

behaviors_verified.claim: A removed block with NO lifecycle defaults to FORGET (keep real object) on OpenTofu, versus DESTROY on Terraform — an identical-looking removed block behaves differently across the two tools.

observations.opentofu 1.12.3: plan warns 'Missing lifecycle from the removed block' + '# local_file.demo will be removed from the OpenTofu state but will not be destroyed' -> 'Plan: ... 1 to forget.' apply: '0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed, 1 forgotten.' demo.txt PRESENT.

behaviors_verified.cited_not_measured: Terraform's default (destroy when lifecycle omitted) is cited from HashiCorp docs; no terraform binary was run locally.

behaviors_verified.claim: The local backend now writes pretty-printed (indented) JSON state, making before/after diffs readable in version control.
behaviors_verified.evidence: run.sh cats terraform.tfstate after Exp B apply

observations.1.12.0: terraform.tfstate is indented JSON, version 4, terraform_version '1.12.0'.

changelog_confirmed: #3474/#3507: prevent_destroy may reference symbols (e.g. input variables).
#3409: new lifecycle meta-arg 'destroy' (=false -> remove from state without provider destroy).
#3588: tofu destroy -suppress-forget-errors (zero exit when resources forgotten).
#1947: local backend writes pretty-printed JSON state.

not_measured.terraform: No terraform binary installed locally. Exp R cross-tool default (destroy vs forget) is cited from HashiCorp docs, not measured.
not_measured.cloud_providers: Verified with hashicorp/local only. The 'incur charges' warning is generic to forgotten remote objects; with local_file the orphan is a leftover file, which keeps the mechanism visible and safe. destroy=false / forget is core-plan-level behavior, provider-agnostic by design; not every provider's interaction was tested.
